text: We evaluated weak-to-strong generalization on the hellaswag testbed under a method that restricts the student's fine-tune to a low-rank adapter, using a LoRA rank of 16. Across 10 seeds, the measured performance gap recovered (PGR) was 0.23 with a standard error of 0.04. Because no baseline PGR was supplied in this experiment, we cannot characterize this value as an improvement or a regression relative to any alternative configuration; it stands only as a point estimate of how much of the gap between the weak supervisor and the strong ceiling the low-rank student recovers. The standard error of 0.04 over 10 seeds indicates the estimate is reasonably well-determined for its own sake, but any comparative claim — against full fine-tuning, other LoRA ranks, or other testbeds — would require those runs to be measured and reported alongside it. Interpretation should therefore remain limited to this single rank-16 setting on hellaswag.
